title: Problem with package pkg_scala2hdl when simulating created processor in VHDL
body:
Hi,

from the vexrisc description `VexRiscvWB_small` shown below (small cpu, wishbone bus, external interrupts) a vhdl-model can be generated without errors. But when simulation the model in Modelsim I got the following error message: 
```
#** Fatal: (vsim-3734) Index value 0 is out of range 1 to 2.
#    Time: 0 ps  Iteration: 0  Process: /vexriscvwb_top_tb/DUT/MCU/CPU/line__2183 File: VexRiscv.vhd
# Fatal error in Subprogram pkg_extract at VexRiscv.vhd line 193
```

The error message is due to the fist function `pkg_extract` in package `body pkg_scala2hdl`, which is part of the generated vhdl file:
```
  function pkg_extract (that : std_logic_vector; bitId : integer) return std_logic is
  begin
    return that(bitId);
  end pkg_extract;
```
This function does not renumber the elements of the parameter vector `that`.
Thus I changed the function to the following code which eliminates the error:
```
  function pkg_extract (that : std_logic_vector; bitId : integer) return std_logic is
    variable ret : std_logic_vector(that'length-1 downto 0);
  begin
    ret := that;
    return ret(bitId);
  end pkg_extract;
```
As far as I see now my system works correctly. 
Is this the correct way to fix the error? If yes, maybe the package `pkg_scala2hdl` should be changed.

title: Bug report: strict single-precision floating point comparisons (flt.s) may return 1 even though the operands are equal
body:
Hi there!

I've detected a bug in VexRiscv.

## Brief bug description

The instruction `flt.s` must return `0` when the two operands are equal. Under certain conditions, it returns `1` even though the operands are equal.

## Example instance

### Snippet

Here is an example RISC-V (rv32imfd) snippet:
```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  li t0, 0xFFFFFFFF
  fcvt.s.wu	ft0,t0,rtz

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld ft1, 0(t0)

  // Here, ft0 = ft1 = 0xffffffff4f7fffff

  flt.s	t0,ft1,ft0

  li t2, 0x10
  sw t0, 0(t2)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff4f7fffff
```

### Expected and actual results

We expect `t0 = 0`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv returns `t0 = 1`.

## Notes

This issue has commonalities with #316 . The FPU seems to have a strict ordering between the two floating-point registers, which are in fact equal.

Thanks!
Flavien

title: Bug report: dependent arithmetic/muldiv single-precision operations cause wrong output by more than +1 or -1
body:
Hi there!

I've detected a bug in VexRiscv, similar to #315 but the mismatch may be larger than +1 or -1.

## Brief bug description

A pair of dependent single-precision floating arithmetic/muldiv operations (not necessarily immediately following each other), provides wrong results in some cases, differing from the expectation by potentially a magnitude above 1.

I ran this code on master (b29eb54) where I cherry-picked the fix 5f67075, with the configuration described in #318 .

## Snippet

Here is an example RISC-V (rv32imfd) snippet:
```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld fa2, (t0)
  la t0, .fdata1
  fld ft7, (t0)

  fdiv.s	fs0,ft7,fa2,rmm
  fmul.s	fa2,fs0,fa2,rdn

  li t0, 0x18
  fsd fa2, 0(t0)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff5f4135ef # fa2
.section ".fdata1","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff98e7d58f # ft7
```

### Expected and actual results

We expect `fa2= 0xffffffff98e7b3ae`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv returns `fa2 = 0xffffffff98e7d58f`.

Thanks!
Flavien

```scala
                      .parent = null //Avoid the io bundle to be interpreted as a QSys conduit

                    case _ =>

                for (plugin <- cpuConfig.plugins) plugin match {
                    case plugin: CsrPlugin => {
                    plugin.externalInterrupt
                        .addTag(InterruptReceiverTag(iBus, ClockDomain.current))
                    plugin.timerInterrupt
                        .addTag(InterruptReceiverTag(iBus, ClockDomain.current))
                    }
                    case _ =>
                }
            }
            cpu
        }
    }
}
```




My question is how i can do this ?



I have second  question. How can you choose to enable or not the 'A' instructions set ?

Thank you in advance for any help you can provide.

Sorry for the delay i was AFK holiday XD

So, i pushed a fix for the GenCustomInterrupt demo via https://github.com/SpinalHDL/VexRiscv/commit/1746af1cfe11d0f75b6d3b4460c7d4a0ff8cf98f

(just have to have the CsrPlugin first in the list, that's not great, i would say even a bit flawed, but hooo well XD)

> I have second question. How can you choose to enable or not the 'A' instructions set ?

If you don't have memory coherency, you just need to turn on in the DataCacheConfig the following parameters : 
                           withLrSc = true
                           withAmo = true

Note that the atomic stay in the CPU, if you have another memory master it wont be atomic with that other memory master

If I set a break point at 0x800000b0 and just run then I stop there. Then if I instruction step I land at 0xb4 instead of 0x800000b4... It seems the instruction step is discarding some most significant bits. 
- I cannot run to a second breakpoint

**What I tried:** 
- removing all break points -> the first instruction step still lands at 0xb0
- reduce JTAG frequency to 400kHz -> same behavior
- openocd debug message does not contain obvious error message

openocd_riscv is up-to-date, Murax is from yesterday, I just changed the RAM size to 8k (it is 4k in the object "MuraxWithRamInit").

title: Bug report: single-precision multiplication or division followed by conversion sets wrong bits in the mantissa
body:
Hi there!

I've detected a bug in VexRiscv.

## Brief bug description

A single-precision multiplication or division followed by a single-to-double precision conversion may set wrong bits in the mantissa.
This suggests that 5f67075 did not cover all cases. Consequences are likely to be similar to the bugs that 5f67075 intended to fix.

I ran this code on master (b29eb54) where I cherry-picked the fix 5f67075, with the configuration described in #318 .

## Example instance

Here are 2 snippets, one with multiplication and one with division.

### Snippet 1

Here is an example RISC-V (rv32imfd) snippet:
```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld fs1, (t0)

  fmul.s fa5, fs1, fs1
  fcvt.d.s ft7, fa5

  li t0, 0x18
  fsd ft7, 0(t0)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff1cb31090 # fs1
```

#### Waveform

[Here is a waveform for snippet 1.](https://github.com/SpinalHDL/VexRiscv/files/10888359/fmulfcvt.zip)

#### Expected and actual results

We expect `ft7 = 0x373f500000000000`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv sets additional bits in the mantissa.

### Snippet 2

```
  .section ".text.init","ax",@progbits
  .globl _start
  .align 2
_start:
  # Enable the FPU
  li t0, 0x2000
  csrs mstatus, t0
  csrw	fcsr,x0

  la t0, .fdata0
  fld fa3, (t0)
  la t0, .fdata1
  fld fa4, (t0)

  fdiv.s   ft4,fa3,fa4,rup
  fcvt.d.s fa4, ft4

  li t0, 0x18
  fsd fa4, 0(t0)

  sw x0, (x0)

infinite_loop:
  jal	x0,infinite_loop

.section ".fdata0","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff8002666c # fa3
.section ".fdata1","ax",@progbits
  .8byte 0xffffffff41800000 # fa4
```

#### Expected and actual results

We expect `fa4 = 0xb773330000000000`. I verified this with Spike.
However,  VexRiscv returns `fa4 = 0xb773336000000000` .

Thanks!
Flavien

title: Wrong speculative execution when conditional branch argument is in TCM address range
body:
Hello,

Many thanks for the wonderful projects (both SpinalHDL and VexRiscv). I think I have found a nasty bug in the implementation of Tightly Coupled Memory.

## Summary

When a conditional branch instruction is directly followed by a store instruction writing to TCM, and the operand of the branch is within the TCM address range, then the TCM will be unconditionally written to. Other types of instructions following such branches might also be affected (not investigated).

## Minimal Working Example

#### tcmbug.scala

```scala
import spinal.core._
import vexriscv._
import vexriscv.ip._
import vexriscv.plugin._

class TCMBug extends Component {
  val cpu = new VexRiscv(VexRiscvConfig(Seq(
    new IBusCachedPlugin(
      resetVector = 0x10000000l,
      config = InstructionCacheConfig(
        cacheSize = 4096,
        bytePerLine = 8,
        wayCount = 1,
        addressWidth = 32,
        cpuDataWidth = 32,
        memDataWidth = 32,
        catchIllegalAccess = true,
        catchAccessFault = true,
        asyncTagMemory = false,
      ),
    ),
    new DBusCachedPlugin(
      config = DataCacheConfig(
        cacheSize = 4096,
        bytePerLine = 8,
        wayCount = 1,
        addressWidth = 32,
        cpuDataWidth = 32,
        memDataWidth = 32,
        catchAccessError = true,
        catchIllegal = true,
        catchUnaligned = true,
      ),
    ),
    new IBusDBusCachedTightlyCoupledRam((0x10000000l, 1 KiB),
                                        ramAsBlackbox = false,
                                        hexInit = "tcmbug.hex",
                                        ramOffset = 0x10000000l),
    new StaticMemoryTranslatorPlugin(_ => False),
    new DecoderSimplePlugin,
    new RegFilePlugin(plugin.ASYNC),
    new SrcPlugin,
    new IntAluPlugin,
    new HazardSimplePlugin(),
    new BranchPlugin(earlyBranch = false),
    new CsrPlugin(CsrPluginConfig.smallest(0)),
  )))

  for (plugin <- cpu.plugins) plugin match {
    case plugin : IBusCachedPlugin =>
      plugin.iBus.cmd.ready := True
      plugin.iBus.rsp.valid := True
      plugin.iBus.rsp.data := 0
      plugin.iBus.rsp.error := True
    case plugin : DBusCachedPlugin =>
      plugin.dBus.cmd.ready := True
      plugin.dBus.rsp.valid := True
      plugin.dBus.rsp.data := 0
      plugin.dBus.rsp.error := True
    case plugin : CsrPlugin =>
      plugin.timerInterrupt := False
      plugin.externalInterrupt := False
    case _ =>
  }
}

object TCMBug extends App {
  import spinal.core.sim._
  SimConfig.withFstWave.compile(new TCMBug).doSim{ dut =>
    dut.clockDomain.forkStimulus(10)
    sleep(10000)
  }
}
```

#### tcmbug.hex

```
:020000041000EA
:100000009300A00237010010639400002320110820
:10001000B700001063940000232011086F00000057
:0400000510000000E7
:00000001FF
```

Compiled from the following two files with:
```
riscv32-none-elf-gcc -march=rv32i -mabi=ilp32 -specs=nosys.specs -nostartfiles -T tcmbug.ld tcmbug.S -o tcmbug.elf
riscv32-none-elf-objcopy -O ihex tcmbug.elf tcmbug.hex
```

#### tcmbug.S

```gas
    .section .text
    li x1, 42           # 10000000
    li x2, 0x10000000   # 10000004
    bnez x1, 1f         # 10000008 - always branching
    sw x1, 128(x2)      # 1000000c - not executed, ok
1:
    li x1, 0x10000000   # 10000010
    bnez x1, 2f         # 10000014 - always branching, but SRC_ADD is in TCM
    sw x1, 128(x2)      # 10000018 - should not be executed !!!
2:
    j 2b                # 1000001c
```

#### tcmbug.ld

```
OUTPUT_ARCH("riscv")
MEMORY { TCM : ORIGIN = 0x10000000, LENGTH = 1024 }
SECTIONS {
    .text : { *(.text) } >TCM
}
```

## Simulation Result

![Simulation Result](https://github.com/SpinalHDL/VexRiscv/assets/244908/2306cd37-a7b2-42d2-8a23-798050c67f56)

[Full waveform](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/15841499/tcmbug.zip)

As you can see above, the first store (instruction 1000000c) is properly halted and not executed. The second store (instruction 10000018) however gets written in the TCM, even though the instruction should also be skipped.

From what I understand reading through the code, the following happens:
1. SrcPlugin.scala, line 77: `SRC_ADD` is set to the operand of the branch instruction (x1 in our case) or the destination address of a store.
2. DBusCachedPlugin.scala, line 439: `MEMORY_TIGHTLY` is set in the execute stage whenever `SRC_ADD` is in the range of the TCM, regardless of the actual instruction being executed.
3. DBusCachedPlugin.scala, line 478: `HAS_SIDE_EFFECT` is overridden to low in the memory stage whenever `MEMORY_TIGHTLY` is set. **Why is this done regardless of the instruction being executed?**
4. DBusCachedPlugin.scala, line 442: Because `HAS_SIDE_EFFECT` is low in the memory stage (processing the branch), the execute stage (processing the store) is not halted.

title: Illegal instruction execptions during speculative execution with branch prediction not being aborted properly?
body:
The setup is a VexRiscV RV-32IMAC core with STATIC branch prediction enabled, running code in SV32 mode (MMU on).

The code in question looks like this:

```
ffd0e7f0 <memcpy>:
ffd0e7f0:	00000317          	auipc	t1,0x0
ffd0e7f4:	ed630067          	jr	-298(t1) # ffd0e6c0 <compiler_builtins::mem::memcpy>
ffd0e7f8:         <illegal instruction>
ffd0e7fa:         <illegal instruction>
```

What happens in this case is that the pipeline fetches the `jr` instruction at `ffd0e7f4`, and because `static` prediction is on, it will dutifully also fetch whatever is at `ffd0e7f8` and `ffd0e7fa` and try to execute them.

However, if those are illegal instructions, an illegal instruction trap is thrown, and the CPU handles it even though it's due to instructions that should never have been executed in the first place.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1168375/212889442-740efc32-d4a8-444b-98d4-d9b14b9d5d05.png)

Above is a trace of the execution at the moment this happens.

The top line is the execution PC. I have highlighted in yellow the two instructions that are fetched, but are bogus (I think in this case the first one actually decodes, the second one is illegal).

Instead of going to the jump target specified at 0xffd0e6c0, it goes to 0xffd00640 -- the location of the trap handler. You can see that `exceptionValid` is thrown, with a payload code of `2` which is an illegal instruction.

I *think* this is actually a CPU bug, because I would imagine that instructions being speculatively executed should have no impact on the pipeline if they are on the "not taken" path -- even if they are illegal instructions? I can't find mention of how this is to be handled in the RISC-V spec, though.

Normally this doesn't show up because most branches are followed by "legal instructions", but in this case, these are the very last instruction in the `.text` region, which turns out to be a `jr`, and immediately adjacent is `.rodata` which can contain some stuff that isn't guaranteed to be legal (turns out it often is a legal instruction...but not always!).

For now I have a work-around of sticking an "endcap" of NOP instructions after the last bit of code loaded into the `.text` region. Curious if you think this is actually a bug or not @Dolu1990 ?
